phaseScreens.notDefended: Not defended – {reason}. The author could not answer; this is not uncontested criticism.

waiting.stoppedText: The session was stopped before this phase finished.

independent.blind: Blind phase: every model receives the identical brief and works in its own request. No model sees another answer, and nobody sees any proposal until all models have finished. Then all proposals are revealed at once.
independent.networkCaption: Each node is one model. Nodes float gently; a node pulses only while its request is in flight.
independent.tooFew: {arrived} of {total} proposals arrived – too few for a council, so no debate or verdict followed. The proposal is readable in the council room, marked as incomplete.
independent.revealed: {n} proposals revealed. Continue with Open Council.
independent.submitted: {submitted} of {total} proposals submitted – contents stay hidden until the reveal.

phaseScreens.author: Author: {model}
phaseScreens.ownClaims: Statements are the model's own claims; they are checked in the 12 Minds Council and Minority Review.

open.waiting: Proposals appear here after the simultaneous reveal.
open.neutral: All proposals in neutral order. No winner is declared in this phase.

minds.perspectivesNote: Several perspectives on the same model are one independent voice when majorities are counted.
minds.waiting: Each perspective reviews all proposals and names concrete, evidence-based objections.
minds.counts: {critiques, plural, one {# critique} other {# critiques}} · {open} not conceded

minority.waiting: Dissenting objections are reviewed separately before any consensus is formed.

why.note: Stored at the start of this council; later changes to the brief or profiles do not change it.

evaluationScreen.confidenceLow: Low confidence – read this verdict with care.

evaluationScreen.hintDebate: Consider “Request more debate” to re-run the missing evaluations, or compare the alternatives before approving.

mainReason.title: Main reason: the evaluation is incomplete.
mainReason.body: {names} could not finish its check. This is a technical gap, not a finding that a proposal fails a requirement.
mainReason.bodyOpen: {names} could not finish its check, so {open, plural, one {# proposal} other {# proposals}} could not be confirmed. This is a technical gap, not a finding that a proposal fails a requirement.
mainReason.nextRepeat: Next step: “Repeat the evaluation” below asks only the missing model again, with your API key and within this council's budget. If it fails again, start a new council – for example with fewer requirements or another model.
mainReason.next: Next step: If it fails again, start a new council – for example with fewer requirements or another model.

evaluationScreen.caption: Mean of independent scores (0–10); ± shows the spread between evaluators.
evaluationScreen.formula: Formula: {formula}. Majority vote (for information only – it never overrides the requirement check): {winner}.
evaluationScreen.eligibleButBlocked: Passes the gates, but cannot be approved in this council – see Final Verdict.

ineligible.declaredUnsolvable: Not implementable: the proposal says itself that the hard requirements cannot all be met
ineligible.hardUnmet: Not implementable: {k} of {n} independent reviewers found a hard requirement unmet

verdictScreen.waiting: The verdict is computed deterministically from independent scores, gates and objections.

notApprovable.s1: does not meet all confirmed requirements
notApprovable.qualifiedBlocked: meets the confirmed requirements, but cannot be approved in this council

verdictScreen.voteWeights: Vote weights (fixed at the start, #140): {list}. Weighted are each model's scores and ranking, not its own proposal; the feasibility check counts every model once.
verdictScreen.notApprovableHint: You can request changes to the brief or reject; a changed brief needs a new council.
verdictScreen.otherGateOne: {proposals} meets the confirmed requirements but did not pass another gate (security minimum, minimum score or a blocking objection) – see Evaluation.
verdictScreen.otherGateMany: {proposals} meet the confirmed requirements but did not pass another gate (security minimum, minimum score or a blocking objection) – see Evaluation.
verdictScreen.gateNote: Details per requirement and evaluator: Evaluation. These are model judgements with reasons, not a fact check.
verdictScreen.archChange: Architecture change: revision v{version} replaced the solution of v1 – the content is not only the author's own.
verdictScreen.archChangeAdopted: Architecture change: revision v{version} replaced the solution of v1 and resembles Proposal {from} – the content is not only the author's own.
verdictScreen.mootSummary: {n, plural, one {# objection against an earlier revision no longer applies} other {# objections against an earlier revision no longer apply}}
verdictScreen.mootItem: {claim} – raised against v{against}; no longer applies to v{current} (not independently re-reviewed)
verdictScreen.conflictText: The proposals conclude, and the independent evaluators confirm, that the hard requirements cannot be met together. A good analysis of that is not a solution: nothing can be built under these requirements. Confirm the finding with “Reject” (no build), or change the requirements – a changed brief needs a new council and a new approval.
verdictScreen.tieText: The leading proposals are too close to call. Choose an alternative with a reason, or request more debate.
verdictScreen.noRecommendation: The council could not recommend a solution. You can request more debate, request changes to the brief or reject.

export.fullTitle: Report plus every requirement check and model call

history.title: Decision history

form.title: Your decision
form.intro: Nothing is developed without your approval. Proposals blocked by a critical security objection, and findings that the requirements cannot be met, cannot be approved for implementation.
form.repeat: Repeat the evaluation ({n, plural, one {# model} other {# models}} without scores)
form.requestChangesS1: Request changes – then edit the brief or requirements and start a new council
form.rejectConflict: Reject – confirm the finding, no build
form.onlyOwners: Only owners and admins can approve decisions.
form.markFavorite: Mark as favourite (no approval, no build)
form.approvePrototype: Approve a prototype / measurement build (not a finished solution)

reasons.needsVerification: Needs verification – the council could not confirm that a proposal meets every requirement. It cannot be approved or built.
reasons.notQualified: This proposal does not meet every confirmed requirement according to the evaluations (or it could not be confirmed). It cannot be approved or built. Change the brief or the requirements and start a new council.
reasons.limitedReview: Too few independent models checked this proposal (at least 2 are needed). It is a provisional favourite and cannot be approved or built. Start a new council with at least 3 models.
reasons.unknownOutcome: This verdict uses a result this version does not know. It cannot be approved or built here.
reasons.conflictOfInterest: Proposal {qualified} meets every requirement, but there is no automatic recommendation: Proposal {blocked} scored higher and was blocked only by the requirement checks of the author of Proposal {qualified} – a decision in its own favour. Start a new council (e.g. with another model) to decide without this conflict of interest.
reasons.architectureCandidate: Architecture candidate – performance proof open: {ids} can only be confirmed by measuring the running implementation. The council confirmed the measurement plan, not the requirement, so no proposal can be approved as a finished solution yet. Mark it as favourite, approve a prototype / measurement build or record the measured result.

why.title: Why there is no approvable recommendation
why.conflict: The hard requirements contradict each other – no proposal can meet all of them at once.
why.violated: {list} not met according to the AI evaluators.
why.violatedCount: {list} not met – {fail} of {total} AI evaluators say so.
why.disputedCount: the AI evaluators disagree on {list}: {pass} say met, {fail} say not met.
why.notEvaluated: not fully evaluated – for {list} at least one AI evaluator gave no valid answer. This is a technical gap, not a finding against the proposal.
why.notProven: {list} could not be confirmed from the proposal text. Not confirmed is not the same as not met – evidence is missing.
why.limitedReview: passed every check, but too few independent AI evaluators took part to recommend it.
why.qualified: meets the requirements; another rule (minimum score, security minimum or an open objection) decides.
why.onlyThese: This is about the submitted proposals only – it does not mean that no solution exists at all.
why.modelJudgement: Judgements of the AI evaluators, not an independent fact check.

next.repeatEvaluation: Repeat the evaluation for the models without a valid answer (costs tokens on your keys; the existing checks stay).
next.addEvidence: Add the missing facts to the brief or as documents (measurements, limits, sources) and start a new council.
next.reviewRequirement: Check whether the violated requirement is really a hard requirement. If not, change the requirement list and start a new council (a new list version).
next.resolveConflict: Change one of the contradicting requirements and start a new council.
next.chooseOther: Choose one of the approvable proposals instead.
next.markFavorite: Mark the architecture candidate as favourite – no approval, no build.
next.prototypeBuild: Approve a prototype / measurement build – not a finished solution.
next.recordMeasurement: Record the measured result with evidence; once every open measurement is met, it can be approved after measurement.

why.architectureCandidate: passed every check, but {list} can only be confirmed by measuring the running implementation – an architecture candidate with the performance proof open, not a recommendation.

followUp.title: Follow-up check (optional, costs tokens)
followUp.intro: The same AI evaluators look again – only at the listed checks, on the frozen proposals. A FAIL is never asked again or replaced. It runs only after you confirm an extra budget.

completion.explain: The evaluators that left checks out are asked for exactly those. The verdict is recomputed afterwards.

targeted_review.explain: Each evaluator looks again at the checks it answered with UNKNOWN, with the other evaluators' evidence as a hint, not as a verdict. FAIL checks stay as they are.

followUp.budgetHint: At least the estimate of {tokens} tokens. It is added to the council's budget and spent on your own keys.
followUp.confirm: I confirm this extra budget on my own API keys.
followUp.error: The follow-up check could not be started.

mark.favorite: Proposal {label} is marked as favourite – not approved; the verdict still needs verification.
mark.prototype: Proposal {label} has an approved prototype / measurement build – not a finished solution and not a regular approval.

requirementGate.title: Confirmed requirements per proposal
requirementGate.intro: A requirement counts as met only if every expected evaluator confirmed every part of it with a reason. PASS and FAIL are stored model judgements with reasons, not an independent fact check.

part.missed: {k} of {n} evaluators expect the limit to be missed
part.across: for {k} of {n} evaluators the range reaches across the limit
part.noEstimate: {k} of {n} evaluators gave no usable estimate
part.noAnswer: {k} of {n} evaluators returned no usable answer

text.noneConfirmed: None of the {n} {other, select, yes {other } other {}}evaluated proposals could be confirmed against all requirements: the evaluations leave requirements open. Not confirmed is not the same as not met.

text.notMet: {id} not met according to {k} of {n} evaluators (model judgement).
text.disputed: {id} disputed: {pass} of {n} evaluators confirm it, {fail} found it not met.
text.notConfirmed: {id} not confirmed: {k} of {n} evaluators could not confirm this requirement.
text.noAnswer: {id} not confirmed: {k} of {n} evaluators returned no usable answer.
text.authorDeclines: The author says this proposal does not meet every requirement (not decisive on its own).
text.architectureCandidate: Architecture candidate – performance proof open: {ids} can only be confirmed by measuring the running implementation; the evaluators confirmed the measurement plan, not the requirement.

requirementGate.buildPendingHint: The proposals name how this is verified (tests, CI). It is not verified yet: the build must prove it before the change counts as successful.
requirementGate.measurementPending: measurement plan named – measured after implementation
requirementGate.measurementPendingHint: The proposals name how this is measured (method, target value, setup). It is not met yet: only measuring the running implementation can confirm it. The requirement stays unchanged.

engineText.noJudgeFailed: No independent reviewer was available – {reason} for every eligible judge
engineText.partialReviews: ({got} of {needed} required independent reviews – no further judge was available)
engineText.conceded: Conceded by the author – recorded as accepted until a revision fixes it (reviewer said: {said}).
engineText.changedAfterConcede: Content changed after the author conceded in {versions} (not linked to this objection).

issue.missing_evaluators: Proposal {label} was scored by {evaluators} of {expected} expected evaluators
issue.vote_disagrees: The majority vote favours Proposal {label}, not the highest weighted score
issue.participant_failed: {model} dropped out of the council ({reason}); its proposal, critiques and scores are missing
issue.unreviewed_objections: {count, plural, one {# objection could not be checked by an independent reviewer and stays open} other {# objections could not be checked by an independent reviewer and stay open}}
issue.single_evaluator: Proposal {label} was scored by a single independent evaluator (only two active models)
issue.requirements_disputed: {failed} of {total} independent evaluators found that Proposal {label} misses a hard requirement
issue.insufficient_evaluators: Only {evaluators} of {expected} expected evaluators delivered usable scores – too few for a council decision; repeat the evaluation
issue.no_debate_contribution: {model} contributed no role review to the 12 Minds Council (every call failed); its perspectives are missing from the debate, but its vote still counts in the Final Verdict if it evaluated
issue.undefended_proposal: Proposal {label} was not defended – {reason}: {count, plural, one {# objection against it stays} other {# objections against it stay}} unanswered, which is not the same as uncontested criticism
issue.phase_shortened: {phase} was shortened to keep the token budget for the Final Verdict; the verdict is based on the revisions available at that point
issue.weighting_changed_winner_both: The vote weights decided the outcome: with equal weights the council would recommend Proposal {unweighted}, weighted it recommends Proposal {weighted}
issue.weighting_changed_winner_unweighted: The vote weights decided the outcome: with equal weights the council would recommend Proposal {unweighted}
issue.weighting_changed_winner_tie: The vote weights decided the outcome: with equal weights the council would end in a tie (weighted: Proposal {weighted})
issue.weighting_changed_winner_none: The vote weights decided the outcome: with equal weights the council would recommend no proposal (weighted: Proposal {weighted})
issue.conflict_of_interest: Proposal {blocked} scored higher but is blocked only by the requirement checks of the author of Proposal {label} – a decision in its own favour, so no automatic recommendation
issue.evaluation_rejected: {count, plural, one {# evaluator restated another proposal's title for Proposal {label}; its scores for it were dropped} other {# evaluators restated another proposal's title for Proposal {label}; their scores for it were dropped}}

replay.title: Council replay
replay.intro: Every entry is a stored event with its real time – nothing is staged or filled in. Step through it, play it back or follow a running council.
replay.withoutTime: {n} stored entries have no time stamp and are not in the replay.
replay.failedNote: Dropped out during the run – the time is not stored, so it is never shown as active.
replay.objectionPending: The decision on this objection has no time of its own – it is shown at the end of the replay.

network.title: Network up to this point
network.empty: No stored questions, critiques, answers or objections up to this point.

table.title: Events up to this point
table.caption: Stored events up to this point, one row each

measurement.title: Acceptance by measurement
measurement.intro: These requirements can only be confirmed by measuring the running implementation. The council confirmed the measurement plan, not the requirement. Record the measured result with evidence; only when every open measurement is met can the proposal be approved after measurement.
measurement.evidenceHint: For example a measurement log, a report or a link. Required.
measurement.error: The measurement could not be saved.

sessionDelete.title: Delete this session
sessionDelete.text: Deletes this council session with all proposals, verdicts, approvals, measurements, builds and the delivery log. The project, its brief, requirement lists and other sessions stay. This cannot be undone.
sessionDelete.exportFirst: Export the report first if you want to keep it:
sessionDelete.stopFirst: This council is still running – stop it first (and cancel an active build), then delete the session.
sessionDelete.external: Already sent reports, draft pull requests on GitHub and backups (until their retention ends) are not deleted by CONSYRION. The month's council count is not reset.
